suggest_mode_values.right_now: can be suggested as an immediate 1-45 min activity
suggest_mode_values.plan_to: evidence is programme-level or needs other people/booking; offer as a plan-ahead idea
suggest_mode_values.avoid: never suggest; kept so the evidence for NOT suggesting it is traceable
suggest_mode_values.reference_only: generic or professional-led evidence row; not a concrete suggestion

meta.note: Instructions are plain-language paraphrases grounded in the dose tested; they are not clinical advice.

activities.name: Listen to calming music you choose
activities.instruction: Put on music you find relaxing and simply listen for a while. Choosing the tracks yourself and listening in order to relax is what the evidence supports.
activities.min_effective_dose: Single listening session (minutes not stated in the meta-analysis abstract; ~20-30 min unconfirmed)
cautions: Many trials in patients, not everyday stress
Non-clinical meta-analysis found physiological effect n.s. (Panteleeva 2018)
Best estimate for healthy users; small
Works best when goal is relaxation (abstract); the boredom/distraction null is not stated in the abstract and was not confirmed (no open full text)
Do not claim music fixes boredom. NOT CONFIRMED: this boredom finding is not in the PubMed abstract

activities.name: Stay on sad music
activities.instruction: Not suggested on its own. If music is chosen while sad, start with a track that matches the mood and move toward a brighter one over two or three tracks.
cautions: Contraindicated for users prone to rumination/depression

contraindicated_for.reason: Self-selected sad music increased depressed mood in people prone to rumination (Garrido & Schubert 2015; not in PubMed)
Same finding

activities.name: Listen to upbeat music
activities.instruction: Play a few upbeat songs you like. People report this helps raise energy, but the evidence is a self-report survey only.
cautions: Self-report survey, not an experiment; abstract names exercise (not music) as the most effective mood-regulating behaviour

contraindicated_for.reason: Arousal-increasing activities do not reduce anger (Kjaervik & Bushman 2024)
Activating

activities.name: Dance freely to a song
activities.instruction: Put on a song and move however you like for about five minutes, in private, with nobody watching or judging.
activities.min_effective_dose: 5 min single session (Campion & Levita 2014, via Koch 2019 full text; single small study)
cautions: Single study, not in PubMed; Koch 2019 meta-analysis coded this study as a small negative effect (d = −0.17) for dance vs its controls; keep it private/non-evaluative
Cycling control did not reduce fatigue

contraindicated_for.reason: Arousal-increasing activity; not shown to reduce anger

activities.name: Join a dance class or dance regularly
activities.instruction: Plan a regular dance class or session. The evidence is for multi-week group programmes, not a single dance.
cautions: High heterogeneity overall (I² = 72.6%) and for dance (I² = 78.0%), but DMT cluster homogeneous (I² = 3.5%); mean programme length 11.4 weeks; group, facilitated — not solo single session
inferior to other exercise for stress

contraindicated_for.reason: Evidence is programme-level (mean 11.4 weeks)

activities.name: Draw something you can see
activities.instruction: Pick an object nearby and draw it for about ten minutes. Focus on the object, not on how you feel.
activities.min_effective_dose: Single short session after a mood induction (minutes not checkable)

activities.name: Draw something that makes you happy
activities.instruction: Draw something that makes you happy for about ten minutes. Skill does not matter.
activities.min_effective_dose: Single session (minutes not checkable)

activities.name: Draw to vent your feelings
activities.instruction: Not suggested: drawing to vent gave no mood benefit over a control task and did worse than distracting or positive drawing.
cautions: BACKFIRE/NULL: avoid as acute mood-repair prompt

contraindicated_for.reason: No benefit vs control (Dalebroux et al. 2008; not in PubMed)
Expressing did worse than distracting (Genuth & Drake 2021; not in PubMed)
Null for acute mood repair

activities.name: Colour a mandala or patterned design
activities.instruction: Choose a mandala or patterned design you like and colour it for about twenty minutes. A structured design works better than a blank page.
activities.min_effective_dose: Single session (~20 min, unverified)
requirements: colouring page and pens (or a colouring app)
cautions: Exp. 1 (n = 88): unguided colouring no better than free drawing; some participants disliked the guiding voice
Not in PubMed: design details still unverified (DOI matches the reference list of a citing PMC article); "preliminary" in title
Let the user choose the design

activities.name: Shape clay or modelling dough
activities.instruction: Knead and shape a piece of clay or modelling dough for a while, making anything you like.
activities.min_effective_dose: Single short session after a mood induction; 30 min in one small study

activities.name: Play an instrument you already play
activities.instruction: Play an instrument you already know for around half an hour, just for yourself with no audience.
activities.min_effective_dose: 30 min (single small study; not checkable in PubMed)

activities.name: Sing with no audience
activities.instruction: Sing along to something you like, on your own and with no one listening or judging.
activities.min_effective_dose: One low-pressure session (15 professional singers)
cautions: BACKFIRE: cortisol rises when performing for an audience

contraindicated_for.reason: Cortisol rose when singing for an audience (Fancourt et al. 2015)

activities.name: Sing with a group or choir
activities.instruction: Plan to join a choir or group sing. This is a plan-ahead suggestion, not something to do right now.
activities.min_effective_dose: Single one-hour choir session (uncontrolled, special population)
cautions: Quasi-experimental; needs a group; not right-now

contraindicated_for.reason: Group activity
Needs a group; not right-now

activities.name: Make free art (collage, markers, paint)
activities.instruction: Spend up to 45 minutes making anything you like with collage, markers, paint or clay. There is no right result.
activities.min_effective_dose: 45 min (uncontrolled study, 39 adults)
cautions: No control group; facilitated by an art therapist (the first author)
Only evidence covering painting/collage; cannot separate media
source_activity_labels: Mixed art-making (painting, collage, drawing, clay, mandala)

activities.name: Therapist-led art therapy
activities.instruction: Reference only: evidence is for multi-session therapist-led art therapy, not a self-guided activity.
cautions: Improvement in 18% of outcomes, 81% no improvement; low study quality; not self-guided

activities.name: Arts engagement (any)
activities.instruction: Reference only: scoping-review evidence that arts engagement relates to wellbeing; no effect sizes.
cautions: Scoping review: no effect sizes or quality grading

activities.name: Expressive writing about a difficult experience
activities.instruction: Over three or four days, write for 15-20 minutes about your deepest thoughts and feelings on something difficult. Expect to feel a bit worse right afterwards; any benefit is small and shows up weeks later.
cautions: Tiny effect; multi-session; the d ≈ 0.15 is a conversion from r, not a figure in the abstract
No immediate benefit; short intervals (1–3 days) between sessions gave stronger effects
Do not suggest for low mood expecting relief
BACKFIRE: short-term distress up, positive mood down

contraindicated_for.reason: Short-term distress goes up and positive mood down right after writing (Baikie & Wilhelm 2005)
Do not offer to someone highly distressed with no follow-up
No significant long-term effect on depressive symptoms in healthy adults (Reinhold et al. 2018; not in PubMed)

activities.name: Write about your best possible self
activities.instruction: Imagine a future in which everything has gone as well as it could, and write about it for up to twenty minutes.
activities.min_effective_dose: Single 20-min session in several included studies (Carrillo et al. 2019, Table 1)
cautions: CORRECTED: the marginal moderator trend runs the other way — fewer total minutes of practice → larger effect (and older participants → larger effect)
Better for raising positive affect than lowering negative

activities.name: Journal for a few minutes
activities.instruction: Write for about fifteen minutes about what is on your mind, including anything that went well. The evidence is for journaling repeated over weeks, so treat one session as a start.
cautions: High heterogeneity (I² 83.8% intervention arm); SORT level B; clinical significance unclear; not single-session
Preliminary; patient sample; vs usual care, lower anxiety and depressive symptoms were reported at 1 month

contraindicated_for.reason: Evidence is multi-week; small effects

activities.name: Read or write a poem
activities.instruction: Read a poem you like, or write a few lines of your own. Evidence is preliminary and from group programmes.
cautions: Small, heterogeneous, likely publication bias; not indexed in PubMed, so authors and numbers remain unverified

activities.name: Knit or crochet
activities.instruction: If you already knit or crochet, pick it up for a while. Evidence comes from a survey of existing knitters.

activities.name: Cook or bake something
activities.instruction: Cook or bake something simple you enjoy. The evidence is for group cooking classes, so cooking with or for someone is closest to what was studied.
cautions: Not solo home cooking; authors call evidence limited
Social benefit depends on the group

activities.name: Eat a meal with someone
activities.instruction: Arrange to eat a meal with someone. Evidence is a cross-sectional survey of habitual social eating.
cautions: Cross-sectional; no evidence located on cooking for others specifically
source_activity_labels: Eat a meal with others / cook for someone

activities.name: Take a photo of something that makes you (or someone else) happy
activities.instruction: Take one photo of something that makes you smile, or one you think would make someone else happy and send it to them.
activities.min_effective_dose: 1 photo/day; effect seen after 3 weeks
cautions: Requires sending the photo to someone
source_activity_labels: Photography (photo to make someone else happy)

activities.name: Do a small creative project
activities.instruction: Spend some time on any creative hobby you enjoy. This suits a good or energetic mood especially well.
cautions: Next-day effect; no evidence it lowers negative affect
Calm/relaxed moods do not show the boost

activities.name: Read fiction
activities.instruction: Read a story for a while as a break. Do not expect an instant mood lift: benefit showed up only after recalling or discussing what was read.

contraindicated_for.reason: No immediate effect of a single reading exposure (Carney & Robertson 2022)

activities.name: Work through a self-help book
activities.instruction: Plan-ahead only: structured CBT-style self-help books over weeks reduced depressive symptoms in adults with depression.
cautions: CBT self-help books, not fiction; clinical

contraindicated_for.reason: Weeks-long, clinical evidence

activities.name: Self-paced moderate exercise
activities.instruction: Do 20-40 minutes of any movement you like at a comfortable, self-chosen pace: cycling, swimming, a fast walk. Stop if you get chest pain, dizziness or unusual breathlessness.
activities.min_effective_dose: Single bout; fatigue falls only if >20 min low-to-moderate (Loy et al. 2013; not re-confirmed); most single-bout studies 21-40 min
cautions: do not promise fatigue relief from a short hard bout

contraindicated_for.reason: Arousal-increasing activities did not reduce anger, g = -0.02 (Kjaervik & Bushman 2024)
Keep it moderate in the last hour before bed

activities.name: Go for a jog or run
activities.instruction: Jog at an easy, self-chosen pace. The low-mood evidence is for regular jogging or walking over weeks.
cautions: do NOT suggest running for anger

contraindicated_for.reason: Do not suggest running for anger: arousal-increasing activities g = -0.02 (Kjaervik & Bushman 2024)
High effort
Vigorous exercise ending within 1 h of bed may impair sleep

activities.name: Take a brisk 10-minute walk
activities.instruction: Walk briskly for ten minutes, outdoors if you can. In one small study this raised energy and lowered tension for up to two hours.
activities.min_effective_dose: 10 min (Thayer 1987, n = 18; energy up and tension down for up to 2 h)
cautions: benefit may fade within ~10 min of stopping
Older single-lab study; exercise covered in depth by other researcher

activities.name: Walk the stairs for 10 minutes
activities.instruction: Walk up and down stairs at an easy-to-moderate pace for ten minutes.
activities.min_effective_dose: 10 min low-to-moderate (18 college women; transient)

contraindicated_for.reason: Arousal-increasing

activities.name: Take 5-minute movement breaks each hour
activities.instruction: Get up and walk for five minutes now, and repeat roughly every hour for the rest of your sitting day.
activities.min_effective_dose: 6 x 5 min moderate walking across a 6-h day (benefit seen at end of day, not after one break)
cautions: benefit seen at end of day, not after one break

activities.name: High-intensity interval training
activities.instruction: Only for people who already exercise regularly: a short interval workout. Evidence is for programmes, and hard intervals feel unpleasant while you do them.
requirements: no heart, metabolic or kidney disease
cautions: regular exercisers only; unpleasant above threshold; not within 1 h of bed
medical caution for inactive users or heart/metabolic/renal disease

contraindicated_for.reason: Arousal-increasing
High effort
Medical caution for inactive users or heart/metabolic/renal disease
Not within 1 h of bed
Above-threshold exercise feels worse, which matters when already distressed

activities.name: Very hard exercise (above your comfortable pace)
activities.instruction: Not suggested as a mood fix: above the ventilatory threshold exercise reliably feels unpleasant. Prefer a self-selected comfortable pace.
cautions: suppress vigorous suggestions in last hour before bed; moderate exercise is fine

contraindicated_for.reason: Arousal-increasing activities do not reduce anger
High effort
Vigorous exercise ending within 1 h of bed may impair sleep (Stutz et al. 2019)
Screening advised

activities.name: Strength training
activities.instruction: Do a strength session with good technique. The anxiety and low-mood evidence is for regular training over weeks.

contraindicated_for.reason: High effort
Programme-level evidence

activities.name: Gentle yoga
activities.instruction: Do a gentle, slow yoga sequence. Slower meditative styles calm more in the moment than power styles.
activities.min_effective_dose: One session (single-session meta-analysis not found in PubMed; unconfirmed)
cautions: citation not found in PubMed (PubMed pass) — paper identity, journal, year and numbers all unconfirmed; gentle styles work better acutely
pooled across calming activities, not yoga alone

activities.name: Tai chi
activities.instruction: Practise tai chi regularly. The evidence is for regular practice over weeks to months, not one session.
cautions: mixed trial quality; no acute anxiety effect of one session
mixed trial quality; "single session showed no effect" comes from the unconfirmed single-session meta-analysis

contraindicated_for.reason: Programme-level evidence; no acute anxiety effect confirmed

activities.name: Qigong
activities.instruction: Practise qigong regularly. Evidence is from a few flawed trials of 1-3 months of practice.

contraindicated_for.reason: Programme-level evidence

activities.name: 10 minutes of stretching
activities.instruction: Stretch gently through your neck, shoulders, back and legs for ten minutes.
activities.min_effective_dose: 10 min after work, repeated over 3 months (no single-session evidence)
cautions: programme-level; untreated control; no acute evidence

activities.name: Walk in a green space
activities.instruction: Walk at an easy pace in a park or other green space. Even a short walk is associated with better mood; the rumination study used 90 minutes.
activities.min_effective_dose: Short engagements give benefits ("first 5 min" not in abstract); rumination evidence only at 90 min
cautions: low-quality evidence; calmness may decrease after outdoor exercise; later update found affect/enjoyment benefit only
anxiety estimate imprecise (upper CI −0.01); high heterogeneity for depressive mood

activities.name: Take an awe walk
activities.instruction: Walk for fifteen minutes somewhere new or wide-open and look for things that feel vast or surprising, as if seeing them for the first time.
activities.min_effective_dose: 15 min weekly for 8 weeks (older adults only)
cautions: Small sample, older adults only; no change in anxiety, depression or life satisfaction
source_activity_labels: Awe walk (look for vastness/novelty with fresh eyes)

activities.name: Spend slow time among trees
activities.instruction: If you can reach a wood or forest, walk or sit there slowly and take in the sights, sounds and smells.
activities.min_effective_dose: Short forest visits

activities.name: Visit water (river, lake, sea)
activities.instruction: Spend some time beside a river, lake or the sea. Evidence is mostly cross-sectional. Take care near water.

activities.name: Do some gardening
activities.instruction: Spend half an hour gardening or tending plants.
activities.min_effective_dose: 30 min after a stressor (30 experienced allotment gardeners)

activities.name: Sit or stroll in nature for 10-20 minutes
activities.instruction: Sit or stroll somewhere with trees or greenery for ten to twenty minutes. If you cannot get outside, look out at something green.
activities.min_effective_dose: >=10 min; most efficient 20-30 min for cortisol (Hunter et al. 2019); a 40-second green view sustained attention in one experiment (not in PubMed)
requirements: outdoors or a window view of greenery
source_activity_labels: Look at greenery / nature view micro-break

activities.name: Get outside into daylight
activities.instruction: Step outside into daylight for a while. Evidence is observational (more daily hours outdoors go with less low mood and tiredness). Use sun protection.
cautions: Lab lighting, not outdoor daylight per se

activities.name: Splash cold water on your face
activities.instruction: Splash cold water on your face or hold a cool cloth to it for a few moments. Skip this if you have a heart condition.
activities.min_effective_dose: Cold stimulus to the face during a stressor (28 adults; physiological outcomes only)
cautions: small; no self-report mood; avoid with heart conditions (general guidance)

contraindicated_for.reason: Avoid with heart conditions (general guidance in notes)

activities.name: Cold-water immersion
activities.instruction: Not suggested: an RCT meta-analysis found no immediate stress or mood effect, and cold immersion carries cardiac caution.
cautions: no control group; RCT meta-analysis (Cain 2025) found no mood effect
not useful as an immediate stress fix; cardiac caution

contraindicated_for.reason: Cardiac caution
No effect immediately or at 1 h (Cain et al. 2025)

activities.name: Take a short nap (set an alarm)
activities.instruction: Set an alarm and nap for about ten minutes, ideally early afternoon. Longer naps can leave you groggy.
activities.min_effective_dose: 10 min of sleep (Brooks & Lack 2006, n = 24, sleep-restricted); 5 min gave few benefits; 30 min caused sleep inertia
cautions: athlete samples; low certainty; keep <60 min
low/very low certainty; late naps may affect night sleep (general guidance)
Sleep inertia just after waking; benefit lasts about 2 h; lab evidence; avoid late-day naps
Set an alarm; longer naps produce inertia

contraindicated_for.reason: Late naps may affect night sleep (general guidance)

activities.name: Coffee then a short nap
activities.instruction: Drink a coffee, then immediately rest for under fifteen minutes with an alarm set. Tested only in a tiny driving-simulator study.
activities.min_effective_dose: 200 mg caffeine + <15 min nap in a 30-min break (12 sleepy drivers)
cautions: Tiny sample; avoid late afternoon/evening, caffeine-sensitive or anxious users

contraindicated_for.reason: Avoid caffeine for anxious users
Stimulant
Avoid late afternoon or evening
Caffeine

activities.name: Slow paced breathing
activities.instruction: Breathe slowly and gently, at roughly six breaths a minute, for five minutes or more. Do not hold your breath for long or breathe fast.
activities.min_effective_dose: One 20-min audio session raised relaxation (Toussaint et al. 2021); HRV rises during and right after one session (Laborde et al. 2022)
cautions: moderate risk of bias; avoid fast/hyperventilation styles
HRV change is not the same as feeling better
brief initial rise in physiological arousal

activities.name: Cyclic sighing (long exhale)
activities.instruction: Inhale through the nose, top up with a second short inhale, then exhale slowly through the mouth. Repeat for five minutes.
activities.min_effective_dose: 5 min/day for 28 days (single trial)

activities.name: Box breathing
activities.instruction: Breathe in, hold, breathe out and hold again for an equal, comfortable count. Repeat for five minutes; keep the holds short.
activities.min_effective_dose: 5 min/day for 28 days (one trial arm; not superior to mindfulness)

activities.name: Progressive muscle relaxation
activities.instruction: Working from feet to face, tense each muscle group for a few seconds and then release it, for about twenty minutes.
activities.min_effective_dose: One 20-min audio session (60 undergraduates)
cautions: effects from training, not one session

activities.name: Guided imagery
activities.instruction: Close your eyes and imagine a calm, pleasant place in detail for about twenty minutes, ideally following an audio guide.
activities.min_effective_dose: One 20-min audio session (60 undergraduates)

activities.name: Take a time-out and count to ten
activities.instruction: Step away from the situation and count slowly to ten before you respond. This is inferred from calming-activity evidence, not tested on its own.
cautions: time-out/counting is not named in the PubMed abstract; not independently verified

activities.name: Venting, hitting things or 'blowing off steam'
activities.instruction: Never suggested: venting and arousal-raising activities do not reduce anger and can increase it.

contraindicated_for.reason: g = -0.02 for arousal-increasing activities (Kjaervik & Bushman 2024); hitting a bag while ruminating raised anger (Bushman 2002; not in PubMed)
Venting
Venting

source_activity_labels: Venting / hitting / intense exercise (do NOT suggest)

activities.name: Mindfulness meditation
activities.instruction: Sit comfortably and rest your attention on your breathing for ten minutes, gently returning to it whenever your mind wanders. Stop if it makes you feel worse.
activities.min_effective_dose: Single session to ~2 weeks gave g = 0.21 on negative affect (0.04 after bias correction)
cautions: not better than active treatments; adverse effects possible
effect may be near zero after bias correction

contraindicated_for.reason: Meditation produces transient adverse effects in a minority (notes Q4)

activities.name: Body scan
activities.instruction: Lie or sit still and slowly move your attention through your body from toes to head. Stop if focusing on the body makes you more uneasy.
cautions: body focus can raise distress in some

contraindicated_for.reason: Body focus can raise distress in some

activities.name: Loving-kindness meditation
activities.instruction: Silently wish yourself and then other people well ('may you be happy, may you be safe') for about ten minutes.
activities.min_effective_dose: Single session to weeks (immediate effect not significant vs neutral visualisation)

activities.name: Self-compassion exercise
activities.instruction: Write or say to yourself what you would say to a good friend in the same situation. Evidence is mostly from multi-session programmes.

activities.name: Write a short gratitude list
activities.instruction: Write down three to five things you are grateful for today. Effects are small and no better than other positive activities.
cautions: modest; not a treatment for depression/anxiety

activities.name: Send a thank-you message
activities.instruction: Write a short message thanking someone for something specific and send it. People usually underestimate how good it feels to receive.
activities.min_effective_dose: One gratitude letter (8-10 min writing)
cautions: may not suit severe low mood [U]

activities.name: Savour a good moment
activities.instruction: Pause on something good that is happening or happened today: notice the details, tell someone, or let yourself show it.
cautions: single recent meta-analysis; larger point estimates vs passive than active controls
source_activity_labels: Savor using varied strategies (be present, tell someone, anticipate/recall, express it)

activities.name: Revisit a happy memory
activities.instruction: Spend ten minutes recalling a cherished memory in detail, with old photos or music if you like.
activities.min_effective_dose: Brief recall task (nostalgia); 10 min twice daily for a week (reminiscence)
cautions: Naturally occurring daily nostalgia can co-occur with negative affect (Newman 2020, U)
Tested as consequence of boredom plus meaning outcome; not a boredom-reduction trial
source_activity_labels: Nostalgic reflection (recall a cherished memory, old photos/music)
Positive reminiscence with imagery or photos/memorabilia

activities.name: Positive psychology exercises (general)
activities.instruction: Reference only: pooled evidence across positive psychology exercises.
cautions: shrinks after bias correction (White et al. 2019)

activities.name: Look at the situation another way
activities.instruction: Ask yourself: what is another way to read this situation, and what might I think about it in a month? Best when feelings are mild to moderate.
activities.min_effective_dose: Single instructed use (lab)

contraindicated_for.reason: Reappraisal is a poor first choice at high emotional intensity (Sheppes et al. 2011)

activities.name: Take a step back (self-distancing)
activities.instruction: Picture the situation as if you were watching it happen to someone else, or as a fly on the wall, and describe what you see.
activities.min_effective_dose: Single instructed use (lab)

contraindicated_for.reason: Cognitive strategies are offered after attention-based ones at high intensity

activities.name: Talk to yourself by name
activities.instruction: Silently coach yourself using your own name or 'you' instead of 'I' ('Sam, you have handled this before').
activities.min_effective_dose: Seconds to 3 min (durations not stated in abstracts)

activities.name: Name the feeling
activities.instruction: Put a precise word on what you feel right now (for example 'tense' or 'disappointed'). If two feelings are present, name both.
activities.min_effective_dose: Seconds per label (lab/neural evidence)

activities.name: Do an absorbing task for a few minutes
activities.instruction: Do something that fully occupies your attention for ten minutes: a puzzle, a game or a hands-on task unrelated to what is bothering you.
activities.min_effective_dose: Single use (lab)
requirements: puzzle, game or task of your choice
source_activity_labels: Psychological detachment activity (absorbing, unrelated to demands)

activities.name: Play a challenge-matched game (e.g. Tetris)
activities.instruction: Play a game such as Tetris at a level that is neither too easy nor too hard, for about ten minutes. Set a timer.
activities.min_effective_dose: Adaptive Tetris session (about 10 min; not confirmed in abstract)
cautions: Too easy = boring; too hard = frustrating; time-box; worry itself was not reduced in the experiment

activities.name: Play a casual video game
activities.instruction: Play a casual game for up to twenty minutes, then stop. Set a timer so it does not crowd out other things.
activities.min_effective_dose: Single short sessions (about 20 min; not confirmed)
cautions: Heterogeneous designs; risk of displacement, so time-box

activities.name: Play a board game with someone
activities.instruction: Play a board or card game with someone. There is little direct evidence for mood or boredom.

activities.name: Sitting alone dwelling on the feeling
activities.instruction: Never suggested: concentrating on the feeling made negative emotion worse, and many people find sitting alone with their thoughts aversive.
cautions: Guided mindfulness differs from unguided thinking

contraindicated_for.reason: Many find it aversive (Wilson et al. 2014)
d+ = -0.26 for concentrating on feelings (Webb et al. 2012)
Same
Same
Same

source_activity_labels: Dwelling on feelings alone (do NOT suggest)
Sitting alone with thoughts, no activity (to AVOID as boredom fix)

activities.name: Postpone worry to a set time
activities.instruction: Note the worry down and tell yourself you will think it through later, in one fixed 30-minute slot today.
activities.min_effective_dose: One 30-min window/day for about a week (not in PubMed)

activities.name: Write a specific to-do list or plan
activities.instruction: Spend five minutes writing down everything unfinished, then note when and how you will do each item. You do not need to do them now.
activities.min_effective_dose: 5 min writing (Scullin et al. 2018, n = 57; outcome was sleep onset)
cautions: outcome is sleep, not felt overwhelm
Lab cognitive outcomes, not self-reported stress
source_activity_labels: Write a specific plan for unfinished tasks

activities.name: Make an if-then plan for the first step
activities.instruction: Pick the smallest first step and write it as 'If it is [time/place], then I will [action]'.
activities.min_effective_dose: One-off plan formation (outcome is goal attainment, not emotion)
source_activity_labels: If-then plan for the first step (implementation intention)

activities.name: Do one small pleasant or meaningful activity
activities.instruction: Choose one small thing you usually enjoy or that matters to you, schedule it, and do it for five to ten minutes even if you do not feel like it.
cautions: figure confirmed in PubMed abstract; CI not in abstract

activities.name: Take a micro-break
activities.instruction: Step away from what you are doing for up to ten minutes: stand, stretch, look out of the window or simply rest.
activities.min_effective_dose: <=10 min (Albulescu et al. 2022)
cautions: little performance benefit after heavy tasks
Highly depleting work may need longer than 10 min
source_activity_labels: Micro-break (step away, stretch, relax, look away)

activities.name: Laughter exercises
activities.instruction: Try a laughter-yoga style session with others or a video. Evidence is from multi-session programmes at high risk of bias.
cautions: all studies high risk of bias

activities.name: Watch something funny
activities.instruction: Watch a comedy clip or show that reliably makes you laugh.
activities.min_effective_dose: Single session of about 9-60 min

activities.name: Take a warm bath or shower
activities.instruction: Take a warm bath or shower for ten minutes or more. The evidence is for falling asleep faster when done one to two hours before bed.
activities.min_effective_dose: 10+ min at 40-42.5 C, 1-2 h before bed (sleep-onset evidence)
cautions: evidence is for sleep, not mood

activities.name: Smell lavender
activities.instruction: If you like the scent and have no allergy, inhale lavender oil from a tissue or diffuser for a few minutes.
activities.min_effective_dose: Often a single exposure (many medical settings; high heterogeneity)

contraindicated_for.reason: Allergies

activities.name: L-theanine supplement
activities.instruction: Reference only: the app should not suggest supplements. The evidence does not validate tea drinking.
cautions: does not validate tea drinking; hydration evidence not found
source_activity_labels: L-theanine (supplement dose, not a cup of tea)

activities.name: 5-4-3-2-1 grounding
activities.instruction: Name five things you can see, four you can touch, three you can hear, two you can smell and one you can taste. This is practice-based, not evidence-based.

activities.name: Call someone instead of texting
activities.instruction: Call or video-call a friend or family member for a few minutes. It usually feels less awkward than people expect; a text is fine if a call feels like too much.
activities.min_effective_dose: Single conversation
cautions: People over-predict awkwardness; offer text fallback for socially anxious users
Calls were received, not self-initiated; older/homebound sample

contraindicated_for.reason: Offer the text fallback

source_activity_labels: Voice or video call a friend/family member (instead of texting)

activities.name: Send a 'thinking of you' message
activities.instruction: Send a short, unexpected message to someone you have not spoken to for a while. People appreciate it more than senders expect.
activities.min_effective_dose: Single message (outcome is recipient appreciation)
cautions: Outcome is recipient appreciation, not sender loneliness
source_activity_labels: Send an unexpected "thinking of you" message

activities.name: Have a brief friendly chat
activities.instruction: Exchange a few genuine words with a barista, neighbour, classmate or colleague.
activities.min_effective_dose: About 1 minute interaction (single field experiment; not in PubMed)
cautions: Not for everyone: context/safety; socially anxious users may find it aversive

contraindicated_for.reason: May be aversive for socially anxious users; context and safety matter

source_activity_labels: More weak-tie interactions in the day (acquaintances, classmates)
Talk to a stranger (e.g., on commute)

activities.name: Question a negative social assumption
activities.instruction: Notice one negative assumption about how others see you ('they would not want to hear from me') and write down the evidence for and against it. Evidence is for multi-session programmes.
cautions: Not a single-session dose; high heterogeneity
source_activity_labels: Programme targeting negative social thoughts (cognitive reframing of social expectations)

activities.name: Structured loneliness programme
activities.instruction: Reference only: pooled evidence across structured loneliness interventions.
cautions: Certainty low to very low. Full paper (10.1037/amp0001578, PMID 41129341) is Am Psychol 2026;81(1):36–52 (Epub 2025 Oct 23): 280 studies, 122 RCTs SMD = −0.50 (95% CI −0.60, −0.39)
source_activity_labels: Any structured loneliness intervention (social skills, support, contact, cognition)

activities.name: Passive social media scrolling
activities.instruction: Never suggested: passive scrolling lowered affective wellbeing through envy.
cautions: Outcome is affect, not loneliness; active use not harmful

contraindicated_for.reason: Passive use lowered affective wellbeing (Verduyn et al. 2015)
Same
Listed to avoid in the boredom rule (R08)
Listed to avoid in R04

activities.name: Cap social media at about 30 minutes today
activities.instruction: Set a 30-minute daily limit on social media apps. Tested over three weeks in one student sample.
activities.min_effective_dose: About 30 min/day for 3 weeks (single student sample; not in PubMed)
source_activity_labels: Limit social media to about 30 min/day

activities.name: Learn or try something slightly challenging
activities.instruction: Pick something that interests you and is a little challenging but doable: a new skill, a small project, a lesson. Boredom usually means the current activity is too easy, too hard or not meaningful.

contraindicated_for.reason: Demanding challenge is avoided when tired (R07, R20)

source_activity_labels: Choose an activity that is both attention-fitting and meaningful (MAC model)
Mastery activity (learn something new, small challenge)

activities.name: Do something entirely of your own choosing
activities.instruction: Reference only: having control over off-job time is associated with vigour (correlational). Supports letting the user pick.

activities.name: Drink a glass of water
activities.instruction: Drink a glass of water if you have not had much today. Evidence is only that dehydration impairs thinking, not that extra water energises.
cautions: No verified evidence that extra water energises already-hydrated people

activities.name: Tidy one small area
activities.instruction: Clear one small surface or corner for ten minutes. There is no intervention evidence; skip it if it feels like one more chore.
cautions: No intervention evidence; could add burden

activities.name: Do a small act of kindness
activities.instruction: Do one small kind thing for someone today: help, a compliment, a favour.
activities.min_effective_dose: Varied (single act to weeks)
source_activity_labels: Kind acts for socially anxious people

activities.name: Spend a little on someone else
activities.instruction: If money is not tight, buy a small treat or gift for someone else.
activities.min_effective_dose: One purchase for someone else
cautions: Recall version null in one replication; do not push spending on users in financial stress

contraindicated_for.reason: Do not push spending on users in financial stress

source_activity_labels: Spend a small amount of money on someone else

activities.name: Plan to volunteer
activities.instruction: Look for a volunteering opportunity for the coming weeks. This is a plan-ahead suggestion, not a 5-30 minute activity.
cautions: Not a 5–30 min activity; use as "plan to" suggestion

contraindicated_for.reason: Sustained activity; trials inconclusive for mood

activities.name: Share good news with someone
activities.instruction: Tell someone who is likely to be pleased for you about something good that happened.
activities.min_effective_dose: Single disclosures
cautions: Benefit depends on enthusiastic response; passive or negative responses backfire
source_activity_labels: Share a positive experience with someone
Share good news with a responsive person (capitalization)

activities.name: Fault-finding or suppressing a good moment
activities.instruction: Never suggested: dampening strategies go with lower positive affect.

contraindicated_for.reason: Associated with lower positive affect (Quoidbach et al. 2010; not in PubMed)
Same
Same

source_activity_labels: Fault-finding, distraction, suppression during good moments (to AVOID)

activities.name: Use a good mood to explore or learn
activities.instruction: While you feel good, try something new, learn something or reach out to someone.
cautions: Mixed replication record for broadening effect
source_activity_labels: Positive-mood broadening (use good mood for exploring, learning, connecting)

activities.name: Share a hug or affectionate touch
activities.instruction: Ask someone close to you for a hug, or hold hands for a while. Only with their clear consent.
activities.min_effective_dose: Adult sessions median 20 min (mostly massage-type interventions)
requirements: a willing partner, friend or family member
cautions: Mostly massage-type interventions; consent essential; not for users without a willing partner

contraindicated_for.reason: Not for users without a willing partner; consent essential

source_activity_labels: Hug someone on a hard day

activities.name: Pet a dog or cat
activities.instruction: Spend ten minutes stroking a friendly dog or cat.
activities.min_effective_dose: 10 min hands-on (not in PubMed)
cautions: Requires animal access; watching/slideshow did not work as well; allergies/fear

contraindicated_for.reason: Allergies or fear of animals
